Recorded: the button sits beside the report title, and the export reuses the existing CSV serializer and paging. Before the design rounds, one scope question about the performance row. Its text stays verbatim in the spec either way. Nothing in code or the gather draft shows the row is wrong or impossible; the draft found every row consistent with the table contract.

How should the spec treat `The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s.`?

A) in-scope - the reused serializer and paging must export a 10k-row report in under 60s, checked by a test against a 10k-row fixture.
B) deviates: this sprint does not need the 10k-row, 60s bound, so this gauntlet ships the button and owner column without meeting it.
C) deferred: <a tracker ref, spec path, or URL you name> - the bound moves to that destination, and this gauntlet does not verify it.
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." - correct the row on the ticket if it misstates the requirement.

Recommendation: A - the row is a valid ticket contract with no evidence against it, and a single fixture test can verify it on the paging path you chose, so it should ship in this gauntlet.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
We’ll reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging, with the Export CSV button beside the report title. Dropping the performance row changes an explicit acceptance criterion in acme/widgets#77, so that needs a scope decision.

How should we handle “The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s”?
A) in-scope - implement and verify the 10k-row export completes in under 60 seconds.
B) deviates: omit the 10k-row timing requirement because it exceeds this sprint’s needs.
C) deferred: acme/widgets#77 - leave the timing requirement open in the ticket for later work.
D) repair the ticket - `/skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77` to revise the timing row through the ticket’s confirmation gate.
Recommendation: A - retain the ticket’s measurable performance requirement; the supplied evidence does not show it is infeasible.
